profiles.name: CYT (55, 8-byte frames): any car (raw messages)
profiles.description: CYT box with 8-byte frames: 55 D0..D5 AA from the box (no length, no checksum, AA at the end; the message's command is 55), 55 CMD LEN data CS to it (CS = (CMD + LEN + data) xor FF). Read from Car Info's decoders CytBydF3Protocol and CytBydS6LowProtocol (their deframer, parsePacket). No acknowledgement. Any car: no decoding, raw messages. Also the description of this box type ("box": "cyt-55-fixed").

profiles.name: CYT (55 / 57, no checksum): any car (raw messages)
profiles.description: CYT box whose frames have no head and no checksum: CMD LEN data, CMD 55 or 57 (both ways). Read from Car Info's decoders CytFordProtocol and CytAirFordProtocol (their deframer, parsePacket). No acknowledgement. Any car: no decoding, raw messages. Also the description of this box type ("box": "cyt-55").

profiles.name: Hiworld (AA 55): any car (raw messages)
profiles.description: Hiworld's other framing (AA 55 LEN CMD data CS, same checksum, no acknowledgement), any car: no decoding, raw messages. Also the description of this box type ("box": "hiworld-aa55").

profiles.name: Hiworld (5A A5): any car (raw messages)
profiles.description: Hiworld box (5A A5 LEN CMD data CS, CS = LEN + CMD + data - 1, 38400 bit/s), any car: no decoding, the CAN tab shows the raw messages. The head unit acknowledges every message of the box (FF <cmd>), as Hiworld's app does. Without a car profile the box gets no car type: it repeats its messages once a second and sends no steering wheel key. Also the description of this box type for the car profiles that name it ("box": "hiworld").

profiles.name: KSW MCU (F2 00): any car (raw messages)
profiles.description: The KSW MCU of the Android screens of BMW, Mercedes-Benz…: no CAN box of its own, the MCU decodes the car and sends the values in its own frames F2 00 CMD LEN data SUM, SUM = (CMD + LEN + data) XOR FF, 115200 bit/s; the MCU profile ksw-px6 of LibreHU service (v194 and later) copies them to the car data engine (CAN link « through the MCU »). No acknowledgement. From VincentZ4's « KSW API – Commands » v2.12 (BMW F1x 2011-2012 CIC 8.8/10.25 in, PX6, Android 9) and McuCommunicator (github.com/KswCarProject/McuCommunicator, GPL-3.0; values only). Any car: no decoding, raw messages. Also the description of this box type ("box": "ksw-mcu").

profiles.name: Raise (FD, 8-bit sum): any car (raw messages)
profiles.description: Raise box with the FD framing (FD LEN CMD data CS, LEN = data + 3, CS = LEN + CMD + data), no acknowledgement, hello 81 01 at the start as the PSA Raise profiles do. Any car: no decoding, raw messages. Also the description of this box type ("box": "raise-fd").

profiles.name: Raise (FD, 16-bit sum): any car (raw messages)
profiles.description: Raise box with the FD framing and a 16-bit sum (FD LEN CMD data CSH CSL, LEN = data + 4), no acknowledgement. Any car: no decoding, raw messages. Also the description of this box type ("box": "raise-fd2").

profiles.name: Raise (2E): any car (raw messages)
profiles.description: Raise (RZC) box and most other makers (Simple, Bagoo, Binary, Oudi, Luzheng…): 2E CMD LEN data CS, CS = (CMD + LEN + data) XOR FF, 38400 bit/s; the head unit acknowledges each message with the byte FF and says hello (81 01) at the start, as the Raise profiles do. Any car: no decoding, raw messages. Also the description of this box type ("box": "raise" or one of its makers).

profiles.name: Simple (AA 55, length as command): any car (raw messages)
profiles.description: Simple box whose frames have no command byte: AA 55 LEN data CS from the box, 55 AA LEN data CS to it, CS = (LEN + data) - 1; the length tells the message (6: Audi's misc, keys and steering message). Read from Car Info's decoder SpAudiProtocol (its deframer, parsePacket). No acknowledgement. Any car: no decoding, raw messages. Also the description of this box type ("box": "simple-aa55-len").
